name: Lia Banks
life: Lia learned to read sand density pushing her father's chair. A photograph of an accessible beach usually shows the clean path. She wants people to photograph what happens when the path ends. Sunday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Lia takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: The judging route crossed a soft patch I knew wouldn't hold a wheel. I borrowed three boards from the marina and made the judges take the long route with everyone else.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. Lia has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Lia folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Lia treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To keep the wheelchair route open through the entire judging session.
family: Clyde Darzi is Lia’s cousin raised in the same household. Lia picks the meeting place. Clyde sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The pawned trumpet*, Clyde says, “I repair brass at night. I can give the player a different instrument but I can't transfer those teeth marks.”
connections: Paz Harrow (beach colleague). They move the judging line together and discover there are two different meanings of a reachable castle.

reactions.situation: The judges ask the fastest builder to speak for everyone
reactions.response: Lia asks each child how they would enter their own castle.
